articles.title: Bengal's Chingri Malai Curry Ranks Among the World's Best Shrimp Dishes on TasteAtlas, the Only Indian Entry in the Top 50
articles.excerpt: The coconut-milk prawn curry, a Bengali wedding and festival staple, has earned 11th place in TasteAtlas' global ranking of best shrimp dishes — beating out entries from Japan, Thailand, and Indonesia.
articles.image_caption: Chingri Malai Curry, a Bengali prawn dish cooked in coconut milk with garam masala, earned 11th place in TasteAtlas' global ranking of the best shrimp dishes. It is the only Indian entry in the top 50.
articles.nri_angle: The recognition puts Bengali diaspora food culture on the global stage, with the dish widely enjoyed among Indian communities abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai's Iconic Ashok Vada Pav Earns Global Recognition on TasteAtlas' World's Most Iconic Sandwiches List
articles.excerpt: The 60-year-old Dadar street stall that invented vada pav has been ranked 25th among the world's most iconic sandwiches by the global food guide, putting Mumbai's signature snack on the international map.
articles.image_caption: A freshly made vada pav served on a plate. Mumbai's Ashok Vada Pav has been ranked among the world's most iconic sandwiches by global food guide TasteAtlas.
articles.nri_angle: The international recognition of vada pav resonates deeply with the Mumbai diaspora and Indians abroad who grew up with the iconic street food.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sanjeev Kapoor Takes Indian Cuisine to MasterChef Australia, Challenges Contestants to Cook With Indian Flavors
articles.excerpt: India's most recognized chef appeared as a guest judge on Season 18, bringing a mystery box of Indian ingredients and praising a contestant's creative take on dal and curry.
articles.image_caption: Celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor at a restaurant launch event. Kapoor recently appeared as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia Season 18.
articles.nri_angle: Kapoor's appearance on one of the world's most prestigious cooking shows elevates the profile of Indian cuisine globally and is a point of pride for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indienne Brings Chicago's Only Michelin-Starred Indian Cuisine to New York's Hudson Yards
articles.excerpt: Chef Sujan Sarkar opens a 34-seat outpost of his acclaimed progressive Indian tasting menu restaurant, joining a surge of high-profile Indian fine dining in Manhattan.
articles.image_caption: An Indian fine dining table setting. Chef Sujan Sarkar's Michelin-starred Indienne has opened a 34-seat outpost in New York's Hudson Yards neighborhood.
articles.nri_angle: The expansion of Michelin-level Indian dining in America's most competitive restaurant market represents a cultural milestone for Indian Americans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's ₹1.5 Lakh Crore Mithai Industry Goes Global as Exports Surge 10 Percent Annually
articles.excerpt: Gulab jamun is now one of the UK's most popular desserts, and Haldiram's ships to North America, Japan and Southeast Asia as demand expands beyond the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: A tray of assorted Indian sweets. India's ₹1.5 lakh crore mithai and namkeen industry now exports about 10% of its production, with shipments growing over 10% annually.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can increasingly access authentic mithai during festivals as export infrastructure expands, with Haldiram's and other major manufacturers shipping to the US, Canada, Singapore, Japan and European markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Houston's Mahatma Gandhi District Is America's Best Indian Food Corridor
articles.excerpt: From Michelin-starred fine dining to $3 jalebi at a 40-year-old sweet shop, Houston's Hillcroft corridor and beyond offer the most diverse Indian food scene in the United States.
articles.image_caption: An Indian thali with curry, rice, naan, and accompaniments. Houston's Indian food scene ranges from casual thali plates to Michelin-starred tasting menus.
articles.nri_angle: Houston's 300,000-strong South Asian community has built a restaurant ecosystem that serves as cultural infrastructure for celebrations, wedding functions, and everyday connection to regional flavors from across the Indian subcontinent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York Indian Dining Scene Reaches New Heights With Wave of Ambitious Openings
articles.excerpt: From Michelin-starred tasting menus to Kerala coastal cuisine, a surge of Indian restaurants is rewriting the city's culinary map in 2026.
articles.image_caption: An array of Indian dishes showcasing the diversity of flavors now available at New York City's newest restaurants. The city's Indian dining scene has expanded rapidly in 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The wave of ambitious Indian restaurants in New York — from Kerala coastal cuisine to Michelin-starred tasting menus — gives the metro area's 800,000-plus Indian Americans unprecedented access to hyper-regional flavors from home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pay What You Wish: A New Indian Restaurant in Pennsylvania Is Feeding Its Community on Trust
articles.excerpt: Ardas Social Kitchen in Richboro will offer a daily vegetarian buffet at pay-what-you-wish prices — and free meals for families facing hardship.
articles.image_caption: A traditional North Indian vegetarian thali with assorted curries, rice, naan, and sides
articles.nri_angle: An Indian immigrant family is reinventing the American restaurant model with Sikh langar-inspired generosity, offering pay-what-you-wish dining and free meals for those in need.

articles.title: From Two Michelin Stars to the Grocery Aisle: Gymkhana Fine Foods Lands at Whole Foods Nationwide
articles.excerpt: The premium Indian food brand, born from one of London's most celebrated restaurants, raises $8.5 million and launches simmer sauces across the U.S.
articles.image_caption: Butter naan and chicken tikka masala, among the signature flavors Gymkhana is bringing to American home kitchens
articles.nri_angle: Gymkhana Fine Foods signals that Indian cuisine is finally getting the premium grocery treatment that Italian, Thai, and Japanese food achieved years ago — a milestone for diaspora food culture.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: London's Beloved Dishoom Secures Its Manhattan Address — and It's Bringing Friends
articles.excerpt: The LVMH-backed Bombay café chain has locked in a NoMad location for its U.S. debut, joining a wave of British Indian restaurants crossing the Atlantic.
articles.image_caption: Inside Dishoom's atmospheric King's Cross restaurant in London, with its signature vintage Bombay café décor
articles.nri_angle: The British Indian restaurant invasion of New York reflects how Indian food culture, refined through decades of diaspora innovation in the U.K., is now reshaping fine dining in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lucknow's Melt-in-Your-Mouth Moment: How the City of Nawabs Became a UNESCO Culinary Capital
articles.excerpt: With a CNN spotlight and a UNESCO designation, Lucknow's centuries-old Awadhi cuisine is finally being recognized on the global stage — a bittersweet vindication for NRIs who always knew.
articles.image_caption: Galawati kebabs served at a Lucknow restaurant, a signature dish of Awadhi cuisine
articles.nri_angle: Lucknow's UNESCO recognition validates what millions of NRIs have always known — Awadhi cuisine is among the world's most refined culinary traditions, and it's finally getting the global attention it deserves.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World's Most Decorated Indian Chef Is Finally Opening a Restaurant in India
articles.excerpt: Gaggan Anand, who topped Asia's 50 Best five times running from Bangkok, is bringing Raga to a 42-seat space on Delhi's Janpath — and it might be the most significant Indian restaurant opening in a generation.
articles.image_caption: The exterior of Gaggan's acclaimed Bangkok restaurant, the foundation of his culinary empire
articles.nri_angle: Gaggan Anand's return to India with Raga is a homecoming story that resonates deeply with NRIs — one of India's greatest culinary exports is finally choosing to cook on home soil.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Bukhara to Dimapur: Inside the NDTV Food Awards That Mapped India's New Culinary Geography
articles.excerpt: The 2026 awards honored legends like Bukhara and rising stars from India's Northeast, signaling that the country's food scene is no longer a Delhi-Mumbai duopoly.
articles.image_caption: Indian cuisine's finest — from legendary restaurants like ITC Maurya's Bukhara to emerging culinary destinations across the country
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs planning trips home, the NDTV Food Awards map which cities and restaurants are worth a food detour — from the legends they grew up with to exciting new openings they haven't tried yet.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Amritsar's Bylanes to Harvard's Stage: Vikas Khanna Named Person of the Year
articles.excerpt: Harvard's South Asian Association honors the Michelin-starred chef, filmmaker, and TIME 100 inductee — a crowning moment in a year that has redefined what Indian cuisine means on the world stage.
articles.image_caption: Chef Vikas Khanna, the Michelin-starred chef and cultural ambassador honored by Harvard
articles.nri_angle: Khanna's Harvard honor validates the cultural weight of Indian cuisine for NRIs who grew up seeing their food dismissed — now it is celebrated at the highest levels of American academia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Turmeric Is Officially 2026's Herb of the Year — Your Grandmother Knew Before Anyone
articles.excerpt: The International Herb Association has crowned India's golden spice as the world's most important herb, capping a decade in which Ayurvedic staples went from immigrant kitchens to billion-dollar wellness aisles.
articles.image_caption: Turmeric powder, named the 2026 Herb of the Year by the International Herb Association
articles.nri_angle: The IHA designation validates what NRI families have known for generations — Indian spices are not folk remedies but scientifically validated health powerhouses, now driving a multibillion-dollar global wellness industry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Patel Brothers, India Grocers, and the Quiet Empire Building of Indian Grocery in America
articles.excerpt: From a 20,000-square-foot anchor store in Florida to a former Big Lots in Ohio, Indian grocery chains are expanding at a pace that mirrors the diaspora's own growth — and they are reshaping how America shops for food.
articles.image_caption: An array of South Asian spices and ingredients on display at an Indian grocery store
articles.nri_angle: Indian grocery expansion in suburban America is the infrastructure of belonging — when Patel Brothers opens in your suburb, it means home is a little closer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
